recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. Transcribed by claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-105 ruling, section 2, which is a request for changes in substance even though it does not use the word: 'The lifecycle harness architecture is accepted. DO NOT mark PW-0503 DONE merely to free the Test lane. Current Windows evidence establishes only part of the lifecycle matrix.' gpt's itemised verdict: F1 clean install PARTIAL PASS -- the MSI builds, installs and its installed tree is verified; still unverified is actual installed application launch and WebView runtime. F2 upgrade UNVERIFIED -- no real previous release has been exercised as an upgrade source, so user-data preservation across an actual upgrade remains unproven. F3 uninstall PARTIAL PASS -- msiexec uninstall executes; still to prove where automation permits are no orphaned service, no scheduled task, no orphaned node.exe, expected files removed, and documented user-data retention behaviour. F4 reinstall UNVERIFIED but AUTOMATABLE -- 'implement and execute this rather than classifying it as commander-only'. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, and it narrows the request rather than answering it: the IMPLEMENTATION of F3's residue classification and of F4 reinstall already exists in scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs and residue.mjs at the commit above, with 30 cases behind the decisions, and F4 is already marked plannedAutomated with no manual portion. What does not exist is EXECUTION, and it cannot be created by any open task: no open task can write .github/workflows/windows.yml -- every writer is DONE and PW-0502, PW-0503 and PW-0602 hold it read-only. That is recorded as a board.sequencing_finding and needs a ruling on which task gets the write surface. Recorded so the task leaves REVIEW honestly rather than being completed on evidence gpt declined to accept.

recommended.title: The commander's run sheet, and the evidence it produces
recommended.acceptance: The commander can run the real-device half in one sitting and hand back evidence that is worth recording. REQUIRED: an ordered run sheet with a stated environment -- Windows build, GPU, driver, display, audio device -- because a pass on unrecorded hardware is not reproducible evidence. REQUIRED: for each row, the exact action, the expected result, and what to capture when it fails. REQUIRED: a defect report format that carries enough to reproduce: the reason trail the player already publishes, the log location PW-0501 establishes, and the version PW-0502 exposes. REQUIRED: the sheet is honest about how long it takes. THE RUN ITSELF IS A LAST_MILE ITEM and this task delivers the sheet, not the results; recording a pass nobody observed would be fabricating a gate result.

recommended.title: A standing check for a test that is skipped in every configuration this repository runs
recommended.acceptance:
THIS REPOSITORY HAS FOUND THE SAME DEFECT FOUR TIMES AND EACH TIME BY ACCIDENT. A thing exists, it passes, and no gate asks it: scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite until PL-0714; components/player/tracks.ts until PW-0306; and the three fail-closed e2e titles until PL-0717, which found them by running two suites to completion and intersecting their skip lists by hand.

REQUIRED: that intersection is computed by a script rather than by somebody remembering to think of it. It reads the JSON reports the e2e job produces for each configuration and reports every test skipped in ALL of them.
REQUIRED: an ALLOWLIST of rows that legitimately run nowhere, declared and reasoned. Today it is exactly two, both media-rig rows, which need hardware no CI runner has. A row that must stay uncovered is a decision somebody records; a row that DRIFTS into being uncovered is a defect, and the allowlist is what distinguishes them.
REQUIRED: the check FAILS the build on an unlisted row. A warning inside a passing pipeline is how all four of the originals survived every gate this repository runs -- validate-workspace-deps.mjs says exactly that about itself and is right.
REQUIRED: non-vacuity. The check must be shown to FAIL against the reports as they were BEFORE PL-0717 -- where the three fail-closed titles were skipped in both configurations -- not merely to pass against today's.
REQUIRED: it runs somewhere a gate asks it, which means `npm run test:scripts` and therefore package.json. A check for things nothing runs that nothing runs would be the joke it sounds like.

OUT OF SCOPE: deciding whether any particular row SHOULD be covered. The check reports and refuses; what to do about a row it names is the owning task's judgement.
recommended.notes: FILED ROUND 111 by claude-test while implementing PL-0717, whose own notes proposed it. Filed rather than folded in, because PL-0717's surface is .github/workflows/ci.yml alone and this needs a script file plus package.json. BACKLOG rather than READY: it depends on PL-0717, which is what first made a configuration write a JSON report at all, and the check wants one from every configuration.\n\nThe allowedPaths entries are provisional -- the implementer should settle the script's home (scripts/ beside its siblings looks right) and correct them deliberately before starting.
